title: Loaded Potato Skins
shortDescription: Crispy skins with bacon, cheddar, and sour cream for ten
subtitle: Crispy skins with bacon, cheddar, and sour cream for ten
description: Baked potatoes are halved, scooped, and crisped until the skins shatter. Each shell is loaded with bacon, cheddar, and green onion, then broiled until bubbly. Sour cream and hot sauce finish at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Loaded Potato Skins in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Bake the potatoes
steps.instruction: Scrub potatoes, pierce with a fork, and bake at 400°F on a sheet pan until fork-tender, about 50–60 minutes. Cool until safe to handle before scooping. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Scoop and crisp the skins
steps.instruction: Halve potatoes lengthwise and scoop flesh leaving quarter-inch shells. Brush inside and out with melted butter, season with salt and paprika, and bake at 425°F until edges crisp, about 15 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Cook and crumble bacon
steps.instruction: Bake bacon on a rack at 400°F until fully crisp, about 18 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble into bite-size pieces once cool enough to handle. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Load and broil
steps.instruction: Fill each skin with cheddar and bacon. Broil on high 2–3 minutes until cheese bubbles and edges brown. Watch closely—broilers turn skins from perfect to burnt in seconds. Target oven/smoker temperature: 500°F. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Loaded Potato Skins onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Top and serve loaded skins
steps.instruction: Top with green onion and serve sour cream and hot sauce on the side. Verify shells are steaming hot in the center before putting the tray on the table.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Loaded Potato Skins — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Save scooped potato flesh for tomorrow's soup or mash—do not waste the insides.
A light dusting of cornstarch on shells before the second bake adds extra shatter.
Pre-broil shells without cheese if you need to hold more than 30 minutes before service.
tonightSpread: Two sheet pans of loaded skins with sour cream, hot sauce, and extra bacon bits.
Celery sticks and ranch for crews who want something green between rich bites.
leftovers: Re-crisp in a 425°F oven 5 minutes—microwaving turns skins rubbery.
Chop and fold into a breakfast hash with the saved potato flesh and eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Potato skins are finger food that feels indulgent without slowing down service. They reheat in a hot oven between periods and disappear fast during movie nights or playoff games.
mealPrepNotes: Bake potatoes the night before and store scooped shells on sheet pans with parchment. Cook bacon ahead and crumble into labeled containers. Assemble skins up to 2 hours before the final broil.
